newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude rises, paper curve in backwardation.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude rises, paper curve in backwardation.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude rose on the paper market on Monday with intermonth spreads and CFDs edging further into backwardation as speculation grew of a tighter physical market in June, traders said.
There were no Brent deals reported on the physical market early in the day but a major trader said that if any should be done they would be at a premium to July Brent.
"If there's going to any deals today they should be at July (Brent) plus something," he said.
IPE crude futures gained sharply. By 1220 GMT, June Brent was at $19.12 a barrel, 19 cents higher than Friday's close.
Brent intermonth paper spreads firmed further.
Jun/Jul, which was the focus of early activity on Monday, traded at +10, +11 and +12 cents after trading twice at +3 cents and once at +8 cents in the U.S. aftermarket on Friday.
"Everybody is looking at Jun/Jul. It began the day at +8/+10 cents, went up to +13/+16 cents, then went down to +8/+10 cents and now it is actually +8/+11 cents," a trader said.

Jul/Aug also slipped further into backwardation to talk at +2/+4 cents after trading at flat and +2 cents in late U.S. trade. "The spreads are rising with vengeance...They tend to go in jerks, the market is on a roll upwards," one trader said.
"It has tried the downside and now we're going upward, and the spreads will go with it," he added.

"There's a lot of focus now on the maintenance programmes in June and people are suddenly feeling that the market could be tight for June for North Sea (crudes) ...that will turn prices up, Dated (Brent) and everything else," he added.
Brent contracts for difference also firmed, with a May 27-30 versus Jun 2-6 traded at +3 cents.
This week's CFDs gained 13 cents to be offered July Brent +5 cents, and May 19-23 were bid July Brent -4 cents, 10 cens up on Friday's level.
A June 2-6 traded at July -9 cents, a gain of four or five cents over its Friday levels.
At least one Brent cargo was turning wet on Monday with a loading date of May 27-29, traders said.

In the Mediterranean, traders said the market was very qieut with no fresh talk on sour grades as two Russian Urals deals at Dated Brent -$1.35 and -$1.18 respectively on Friday pushed the market down.

A Mediterranean refiner said he bought on Friday a 60,000 tonne cargo loading May 12 or 13 at Dated Brent -$1.15 but because the seller will suffer demurrhage charges of 20-30 cents per barrel for a week due to delayed delivery, the seller would receive Dated Brent -$1.35. "The market is very, very quiet. People are waiting for third decade May (Urals) cargoes to be shown," the refiner said, adding that talk was also very thin.

"On Friday those two deals really affected the market...they pushed it down," he said. "Now everybody is trying to understand where the market for sour (crude) is so there are no new, fresh numbers out."
